mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate over the past month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings declines and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market reactions to employment data.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises over the past month, or the Rank IC over the past 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1000 thousand units signals a severe housing market contraction, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to spillover effects on consumer spending and financial sector stress.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 1000, SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and retail sales indicates a broad-based economic contraction driven by weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue visibility.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: When both INDPRO and RSAFS decline from prior month, SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary easing cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS below 4.5% and declining), the S&P 500 typically experiences positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower discount rates boosting equity valuations and improved risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.5 and FEDFUNDS declines from prior month
failure_condition: In monetary easing cycles (as defined by the trigger), SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) over the past month indicates increasing price pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to the expectation of tighter monetary policy and reduced real earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises over the past month, or the Rank IC over the past 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in total nonfarm employment below 138,000 thousand persons signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate hiring slowdowns.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS falls below 138,000, SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and low inflation (CPIAUCSL below 2.5%) indicates a supportive monetary policy environment that boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved risk-reward dynamics.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines from prior month and CPIAUCSL < 2.5
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL < 2.5, SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by unemployment rate below 5.0%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to overvaluation and the expectation of monetary tightening as the economy approaches full capacity.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions (UNRATE < 5.0), SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.
